scene.headline: Life had lost the
metadata: ON THE SPECIES OF ELEPHANTS, LIVING AND FOSSIL · 1796

counter.label: elephants in Cuvier's memoir known only as fossils

connections.why: The revolutionary Convention made the Paris Muséum in 1793, and the Republic's conquest of the Netherlands brought it the stadholder's elephant skulls that Cuvier compared in 1796.

Lamarck, Cuvier's colleague at the Muséum, read the same fossils as evidence that species change; Cuvier refused transmutation, and his eulogy of Lamarck in 1832 mocked the theory as fit to amuse a poet.

Cuvier named Megatherium in 1796 and accepted that it wore armor, so Darwin gave it the bony plates he found at Punta Alta, plates Owen gave to glyptodonts in 1839; Darwin's quiet extinctions in the Pampas went against Cuvier's revolutions.
